tools.name: list_organizations
tools.description: List the Flagbearer organizations you belong to. Start here to find an organization's ID. This connection only covers the organizations listed. If the project's application isn't in any of them, tell the user before writing flag code, and ask them to reconnect and approve the right organization.

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: List the applications in an organization. Flags belong to an application.

tools.name: list_flags
tools.description: List an application's feature flags with whether each is on, and its rollout percent, in every environment.

tools.name: create_flag
tools.description: Create a feature flag in an application. It starts off in every environment; use set_flag to turn it on. The key is what code checks, like new-checkout.

tools.name: set_flag
tools.description: Turn a flag on or off in one environment, by flag key and environment key. When turning a flag on, rolloutPercent says who gets it: 100 for everyone, or a percentage of users. Ask the user whether it should be on for everyone. Without rolloutPercent it's 0, which turns it on only for the environment

tools.name: generate_flag_types
tools.description: The text of a TypeScript file listing an application's flag keys, so a misspelled key is a type error and editors autocomplete keys. Write the returned text to the path exactly as it is, and commit it. Only for TypeScript projects using @flagbearer/web (React and browser apps), @flagbearer/node or @

tools.name: get_user_flags
tools.description: What a user should have got for every flag in one environment, by email or user key, with the reason (off, tester or rollout and their bucket), what their SDK reported that UTC day (seen), and any changes that day that flipped their result. Use it when a bug report says a feature stopped working, or

tools.name: get_sdk_docs
tools.description: The current Flagbearer SDK docs for a platform (react, react-native, ios, android, browser, node, python, go, java, dotnet, ruby, rust, cpp or php), plus one environment's SDK address and public client key. Call this before writing code that checks a flag, and follow it.

tools.name: check_sdk_setup
tools.description: What looks wrong with how an application's SDKs are set up, per environment, from what they sent in the last day: flags the code checks that don't exist, wrong or leaked keys, old SDK versions, and environments nothing has connected to. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.flagbearer.dev" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_user_flags · Private data: generate_flag_types · Public sink: set_flag, get_user_flags.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_user_flags · Private data: generate_flag_types · Public sink: set_flag, get_user_flags

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
